A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the downsizing of ellipticals is driven by a combination of two processes: a positive feedback from the growth of the central black hole, and a negative feedback from the stellar population.
the downsizing of ellipticals is a consequence of the downsizing of the AGN activity.

the observed overabundance of [Mg/Fe] is a natural outcome of the hierarchical growth of galaxies in the context of a cosmological model with a cosmological constant and cold dark matter, and is not the result of any specific feedback process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the downsizing of ellipticals, as observed in the anti-hierarchical growth of their supermassive black holes and the anti-hierarchical star formation history, are both intimately linked to the growth of the central black hole and to the feedback that it produces in the early stages.
the overabundance of magnesium relative to iron in the nuclei of elliptical galaxies can be explained without the need of invoking a top-heavy initial mass function for stars.

the overabundance of [Mg/Fe] observed in the nuclei and haloes of bright ellipticals is not due to a top-heavy initial mass function, but to a combination of a top-heavy IMF at early epochs, when the supermassive black hole was growing, and a bottom-heavy IMF at later epochs, when the star formation was triggered by the black hole feedback.
